# E0402: overlapping `inout` arguments

Two places that one call modifies can't overlap, since the result would depend on which one is written back last. Use a method made for it, such as `xs.swap(i, j)`, or copy one of them first.

- Rule: [`modes.overlapping-inout`](../../reference/13-modes.md#modes.overlapping-inout)
- Reported at: the later of the two overlapping places.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `analyses` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0402:7
fn swap(inout a: i64, inout b: i64) {
  let t = a
  a = b
  b = t
}

fn mixed(inout xs: List<i64>) { swap(inout xs[0], inout xs[1]) }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn mixed(inout xs: List<i64>) { xs.swap(0, 1) }
```

## What the compiler prints

```text
── OVERLAPPING `inout` ARGUMENTS ───── E0402_names_of_one_when.lt:12:33  [E0402]

`b` may reach the value of `a`, which this call already modifies:

  12 │     both(inout a.balance, inout b.balance)
     │                                 ^^^^^^^^^

Two places that one call modifies can't overlap, since the result would depend
on which one is written back last. Use a method made for it, such as `xs.swap(i,
j)`, or copy one of them first.
```
